einstellungen.text: The whole hospital suddenly goes dark. And outside, the sky is glowing green.
Three seconds. Four. You can hear your own heartbeat.
Then something rumbles deep down in the basement.
The generators kick in. The lights flicker back on. Grandpa's monitor starts beeping again.
Mom laughs. A little too loud. Out of pure relief.
And then you all look out the window.
When a solar storm hits the Earth, the air starts to glow. Northern lights.
Normally you only see them far up north. But two years ago, in May, you could see them all over Germany.
Lina presses her nose against the glass. “That's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen.”
Then Grandpa opens his eyes. He turns his head toward the window.
“I wanted to see that my whole life. And now I get to see it with you.”
Nobody looks at their phone. There isn't one that works anyway.
Dad tells you how Grandpa taught him to ride a bike. Backwards. By accident.
You laugh until your stomach hurts. Right in the middle of the hospital.
Later, you're standing outside with Lina and Ben on the hill behind the hospital.
Ben says, “Without the outage, we would've missed this.”
Then something vibrates in your jacket pocket.
Your phone. One single bar. And a message that's been stuck for three days.
